_readme: EVERY piece of text on the site lives in this file. Edit it here, save, done —
you never need to open App.js. `npm start` hot-reloads your changes.
Rules, because JSON is picky:
- Wrap all text in "double quotes". Single quotes are not valid JSON.
- Put a comma between items, but NEVER after the last one in a list or block.
- A literal double quote inside text must be escaped: \"
- No comments allowed. This _readme block is the workaround; the site ignores it.
- Accents and symbols (é — · ≥) can be typed directly. The file is UTF-8.
Adding or removing an entry: copy an existing { ... } block, comma-separate it
from its neighbour, and edit the values. Order in the file = order on the page.
The page is the `preview` block, top to bottom: `name`, `subtitle`, the `about`
paragraphs, the `links` row, then `experience`, `aiWork` and `hardware`.
Two things are NOT here, because search engines and link previews read them
before the page runs: the browser-tab title and the description that shows up
when you paste the URL into Slack/LinkedIn. Both are in public/index.html.
Images live in public/images/. A path of "/images/foo.jpg" means the file
public/images/foo.jpg. Hardware photos are cropped to 4:3 from the centre;
ship them around 480x360.
`prototype` is the draft of the next front page, served only at the hidden
path in App.js (PREVIEW_PATH). Same shape as `preview`, plus a `result` line
per row, `pages` on each PDF and the AI portfolio at the head of `aiWork`. It does not change the front page.

theme._note: The light/dark toggle in the top-right. The label names where you are going, not where you are — it reads "Dark" while the site is light.

preview._note: The whole page: one column, read top to bottom. `links` is the row at the top, after the email. Experience and AI work entries render as one sentence: the bold `name` (linked when it has an `href`), then `text`, then any `docs` as small links. PDFs live in public/docs/, so "/docs/foo.pdf" means public/docs/foo.pdf. `hardware` is the photo grid; images are cropped to 4:3 from the centre. Shelved AI rows (not on the site) are in content.shelved.json.

about: Ethics and social impact are far too often overlooked in engineering. These, along with environmental sustainability, are core to my work. With the advent of AI, it is increasingly important that we act with morality and worldly impact in mind.
Every role I’ve held has been in a domain I was new to, and every time I was owning critical deliverables within weeks.

about: I care about what my work does to people and the planet, and AI makes that matter more. So the AI systems I build keep a person in charge: hwde has someone sign off at every stage, and in autobox no agent merges its own work.
Every role I’ve held was in a field new to me. At Fab2 I designed a 200 W GaN inverter for RF plasma in a day, then took it from schematic to first plasma in three weeks.

items.name: hwde
items.text: an AI PCB engineer, from brief to fabricated board.
items.result: 16 boards designed, 6 ready to order and 2 made. The best run went from brief to an order‑ready board in 13.6 hours, with nobody watching.
items.detail: You describe the board in plain words. hwde researches the parts, picks a topology, draws the schematic, lays out and routes the board, runs the electrical and manufacturing checks, and hands you the files a factory needs. A person signs off at every stage, and ordering always waits for one. Neither made board has been powered on yet.

figure.alt: A rendered circuit board with connectors and a wireless module
figure.caption: lumina‑carrier, a 4‑layer board for a stage‑lighting fixture. It’s one of the two that were made.

items.name: autobox
items.text: an always‑on Claude Code agent box.
items.result: 550 pieces of work landed from 27 August to 20 September 2026.
items.detail: It’s a small computer that does software work on its own. It manages Claude Code agents, and no agent merges its own work: every change goes through the test suite, then a second agent reads it against what was asked for. When a gate fails, it sends out a repair worker by itself, so a red build gets fixed without anyone asking.
